text:
maya: Heads-up — saw a spike in tail latency for small prompts that produce long outputs in eu-west over the last 3 hours. Root cause looks like a big drop in prefix-cache hit rate for several popular models.

sam: Any profiling artifacts? Kernel/batching changes recently?

perf-bot: perf/summary: prefix_cache_hit_rate:
  - us-east-1: 74%
  - eu-west-1: 27%
  - ap-south-1: 31%
  median_token_latency_miss: 120ms
  median_token_latency_hit: 22ms
  recent-deploy: 2026-03-16T21:04Z (runtime v3.8.1)

kevin: What are we using as the cache key currently? I recall we include prompt text + model id + user_locale?

maya: Current key derivation (approx):
```
key = sha256(model_id + '|' + model_version + '|' + prompt_hash + '|' + prefix_len_bucket)
```
prompt_hash = sha256(raw_prompt)  // raw byte for now, no normalization

maya: We rolled a kernel-selection tweak in v3.8.1 that changed chunking for long sequences (smaller chunks to improve throughput). That changed how prefix KV blocks line up in the cache and seems to reduce prefix reuse in eu-west (traffic pattern differences). Also batching heuristic changed to prefer 32-token batches vs adaptive 16-64.

jon: Quick repro: small punctuation/whitespace diffs kill hits because we hash raw bytes. Also language/case differences. If eu-west has many localized prompts with subtle formatting, hit rate falls.

sam: Two angles: 1) improve cache keying (canonicalize prompt before hashing) 2) warmup/replication for cold regions (replicate top-N prefixes across regions or pre-warm via replay).

perf-bot: offline-sim: apply canonicalization (collapse whitespace, strip trailing punctuation, normalize unicode NFKC, lowercase for en) -> eu-west hit_rate uplift from 27% to 61% in simulation (same trace).

kevin: Replication consideration: replicating top prefixes reduces cold miss penalty but increases cross-region sync traffic and memory. Need to pick a small N (top-1k per model?) and ensure keys are versioned so rollouts don't stale them. Suggest keys include model_version tag.

jon: Also watch coherency for model rollouts: if we replicate prefix entries for v1 then switch to v2 you need fallback behavior. Proposal: keep model_version in key and add cross-model fallback routing (try exact version -> compatible variant -> smaller model).

maya: Warmup experiment plan:
1) Implement canonicalizer in the request path (cheap) and run canary in us-east for 24h.
2) Background job: aggregate hot-prefixes (top-1k/day per model) and async-replicate to 2 nearest regions (eu-west, ap-south) with TTL 72h.
3) Rollback kernel chunking change on a small canary host where hit-rate drop is obvious, compare latency.
4) Update routing policy to prefer local cache hits but allow cross-region read-through with quota.

sam: I'll open PRs for (1) canonicalizer + unit tests and (2) hot-prefix exporter/replicator. Will include metrics (cache_hit_by_key_bucket, replication_bandwidth, replicated_entries_count). tagging @kevin for eviction policy implications. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: simulation: replicating top-1k -> eu-west median miss penalty drops 120ms -> 30ms; avg cross-region bandwidth ~ 12MB/min for top-1k (model-dependent).

kevin: Eviction: if we replicate hot prefixes, we should mark replicated entries as "pinned" for a short grace period (e.g., 6h) to prevent immediate eviction. Also ensure LRU counters are region-local.

maya: Action items and owners:
- canonicalize prompt hashing (sam)
- hot-prefix aggregator + replicator (sam)
- eviction/pinning changes (kevin)
- canary rollback test for kernel chunking (maya)
- routing tweak to prefer cached copies then cross-region read (jon)
ETA: start canary tomorrow, results by EOD+2.

sam: I'll open the two PRs this afternoon and link traces.

jon: One more note: add a tiny diagnostic in the runtime to emit prefix_key_sample (first 16 bytes of key) for 1/1000 requests so we can correlate misses without logging full prompt. Avoids PII.

maya: Good idea — please include opt-in flag for customers.

perf-bot: note: benchmark id 20260316-kw-03 attached to the canary job when you run it.

maya: Thanks team — will sync in the standup. :white_check_mark:
